p: there be therefore any consolation in: A most earnest request to remove all those things, by which that great and special consent and agreement is commonly broken, that is, contention and pride, by which it comes to pass that they separate themselves from one another.
Christ: Any Christian comfort.
bowels and mercies: If any seeking of inward love.
same love: Equal love.

Let this mind be in you: He sets before them a most perfect example of all modesty and sweet conduct, Christ Jesus, whom we ought to follow with all our might: who abased himself so much for our sakes, although he is above all, that he took upon himself the form of a servant, that is, our flesh, willingly subject to all weaknesses, even to the death of the cross.
form of God: Such as God himself is, and therefore God, for there is no one in all parts equal to God but God himself.

thought it not robbery to be: Christ, that glorious and everlasting God, knew that he might rightfully and lawfully not appear in the base flesh of man, but remain with majesty fit for God: yet he chose rather to debase himself.

equal with God: If the Son is equal with the Father, then is there of necessity an equality, which Arrius that heretic denies: and if the Son is compared to the Father, then is there a distinction of persons, which Sabellius that heretic denies.
no reputation: He brought himself from all things, as it were to nothing.
form of a servant: By taking our manhood upon him.
Wherefore God also hath highly exalted: He shows the most glorious even of Christ's submission, to teach us that modesty is the true way to true praise and glory.
name which is above every name: Dignity and high distinction, and that which accompanies it.
every knee should bow: All creatures will at length be subject to Christ.
every tongue should confess that Jesus: Every nation.
Wherefore: The conclusion: we must go on to salvation with humility and submission by the way of our vocation.
work out your own salvation with: He is said to make an end of his salvation who runs in the race of righteousness.

For it is God which worketh: A most sure and grounded argument against pride, because we have nothing in us praiseworthy, but it comes from the free gift of God, and is outside of us, for we do not have ability or power, so much as to will well (much less to do well), except only by the free mercy of God.
to will and to do of: The reason why we are not statues; and yet we do not will well by nature, but only because God has made of our wicked will a good will.

Do all things without murmurings and: He describes modesty by the contrary effects of pride, teaching us that it is far both from all malicious and secret or inward hatred, and also from open contentions and brawlings.
That ye may be blameless and: To be short, he requires a life without fault, and pure, so that being enlightened with the word of God, they may shine in the darkness of this world.
word of life: The Gospel is called the word of life, because of the effects which it produces.

that I may rejoice in the: Again he urges them forward, setting before them his true apostolic care that he had for them: in addition comforting them to the end that they should not be sorry for the greatness of his afflictions, no, not even if he should die to make perfect their sacrifice with his blood, as it were with a drink offering.

sacrifice and service of your faith: As if he said, I brought you Philippians to Christ, and my desire is that you present yourselves a living sacrifice to him, and then it will not grieve me to be offered up as a drink offering, to accomplish this your spiritual offering.

But I trust in the Lord: Moreover, he strengthens and encourages their minds both by sending back Epaphroditus to them, whose fidelity towards them, and great pains in helping him, he commends: and also promising to send Timothy shortly to them, by whose presence they will receive great benefit. And he hopes also himself to come shortly to them, if God wills.
good comfort: May be confirmed in the joy of my mind.
all seek their own: The most part.
work of Christ he was nigh: He calls here the work of Christ the visiting of Christ, being poor and in bonds in the person of Paul.
